text: ...that is hers. Put it down. No. Play it. Play it again. I haven't heard it in five years.
No. No, not today. Not tonight.

Laboratory diary, Kaltenbrunn, the eleventh of December, nineteen thirty-eight. The specimen from shaft four is... remarkable. It is warm in the hand. It makes a sound like a held breath. Emil says it is only piezoelectric. Emil is very sure of everything until he isn't.

The fourteenth of February, nineteen thirty-nine. Liesl died at four in the morning. Diphtheria. A membrane across her throat. I am a doctor. I could do nothing. There is a man in the Gospel who was four days in his grave, and his sisters had only to ask. I have asked. The stone hummed all night. I listened to it, so I would not have to listen to the silence in her room.

Subject seven-forty walked. Four days from the death, to the hour, as they all do; near the heart, less. Not hunger, not at first. For one minute it looked for something. It went to the window. They remember. It is in the blood, Emil, not in your glass. The glass only answers it, and keeps what answers. I have named it in the files for a man who was four days dead and came home. Lazarusblut. Liesl's last impulse was to call for me. I was there when she died. I heard it. If the impulse remains, then she remains, somewhere in the glass. I only need it louder.
Hush. Hush now. I've got you. We'll find somewhere quieter.
Emil. You'll follow me. You always do. North, to the sea.
Emil, I know you're listening. You always were a coward with a radio.
Do you know what I hear in the heart? Footsteps. Small ones. Running down a hallway. Every night.
You there, the Polish girl. Your brother is in there too. Tomasz. Yes, I know the name. I know every name. You could hear him again.
Lieutenant Ashworth. London wants a piece of it too, don't they? Ask your lieutenant what she carries home.
Please. Please. She is seven years old. She has been seven years old for five years.
You've broken her toy. She took that drummer to bed every night. It doesn't matter. Things break. That's what I've been trying to undo.

Emil has told you to kill the heart. Has he told you what is in it? Thousands. Every miner, every soldier, every villager you have "quieted" tonight. Their last moments, kept. You are not killing monsters. You are burning a library.
Diary, the ninth of February, 1939. She asked me yesterday if the stars were cold. Today I couldn't answer anything at all.

The glass does not make the hunger. The hunger was in the blood before the glass ever came out of the salt. I have named it for a man who was four days dead and came home: Lazarusblut. If I can make the last impulse love instead... then they're not monsters. They're kept.
You are standing in the heart of my work, soldiers. Please. Wipe your feet.
Emil thinks he's betraying me. He's only betraying himself. He always did lack conviction.
Liesl. Mama is coming. Mama is nearly finished.
Fineness twelve microns. Through the mill once more. The dust must float, not fall.
Near the Heart it no longer waits four days. Minutes. Write it down: minutes.
The canisters go east. Return to sender. That was the General Staff's phrase, not mine.
Weather station, confirm the wind.
Liesl. Mama is here. Count to a hundred.
So. Emil's soldiers. You've woken the heart. Do you feel it? It's not angry. It is listening. Please, be careful what you say to it.
Stop. Stop this. You don't understand what you're doing!
Liesl, run. Run to Mama. Run!
Mahlknecht! Protect it!
